cultural.vision_reason: This is a hand-woven strip-woven cotton cloth in a checkerboard pattern with supplementary weft motifs, sewn from narrow strips typical of Kente-style weaving associated with the Ashanti of Ghana. The construction and pattern are consistent with the claimed ethnicity.

physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: Man’s wrapper (Kente cloth), composed of 25 narrow strips of imported blue and white cotton thread, hand-woven and hand-sewn together along the selvedges. Each strip has an identical patter, which runs consistently along the entire length (there is therefore no variation in design at the ends). The warp is of white cotton, through which run five thin lines of blue. The weft is white, with three uniform blocks from a second pair of heddles framing two bands of a zig-zag pattern formed from discontinuous supplementary weft. The weft pattern blocks alternate evenly with plain warp-faced sections and have been sewn together so that the plain and pattern blocks alternate along and across the cloth. The warp ends have been hemmed by machine.
